title: Temurah 24
description: Rabbi Hoshaya on two sin offerings set aside as a guarantee and whose view it fits, Rav Pappa’s correction of Rav Shimi bar Ziri’s baraita, why one may not flay a firstborn or disqualified consecrated animals from the feet, and, as chapter 4 ends and chapter 5 begins, how one employs artifice to keep a firstborn from the priest by consecrating it in the womb.
topics: 🐐 Rabbi Hoshaya: of two sin offerings set aside as a guarantee, one atones and the other grazes
❓ Whose view is it? Not the Rabbis’, not Rabbi Shimon’s, but Rabbi’s, tested by Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
🎲 The Yom Kippur goats, Rav’s “living animals are not rejected” and “a mitzva with the first”
📜 Rav Shimi bar Ziri’s baraita and Rav Pappa’s a fortiori correction
🔪 No flaying from the feet: on a Festival, a firstborn, disqualified consecrated animals
⚖️ Rav Ḥisda: Beit Shammai and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon; reasons from Rav Mari, the West and Rabbi Yosei bar Avin
📖 Hadran: chapter 4, Vlad Ḥatat, ends; chapter 5, Keitzad Ma’arimin, begins
🐄 Artifice with a firstborn: consecrating the fetus, and Rav Yehuda on a blemish before birth

a1.he: אֲבָל בִּתְרֵי סִדְרֵי לָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a2.he: אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא: הַמַּפְרִישׁ שְׁתֵּי חַטָּאוֹת לְאַחְרָיוּת, מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן, וַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ רוֹעָה.

a3.he: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן — הַשְׁתָּא הַמַּפְרִישׁ לְאִיבּוּד, אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן לָאו כְּאִיבּוּד דָּמֵי, לְאַחְרָיוּת מִיבַּעְיָא?!

a4.he: אֶלָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת!

a5.he: אֶלָּא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי, כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי בְּאִיבּוּד — אֲבָל אַחְרָיוּת לָא.

a6.he: תְּנַן: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת, וַהֲרֵי הִיא בַּעֲלַת מוּם — מוֹכְרָהּ, וּמֵבִיא אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אִם קָרְבָה שְׁנִיָּה קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטָה רִאשׁוֹנָה — תָּמוּת, שֶׁכְּבָר כִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ.

a7.he: קָא סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כְּרַבִּי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ, וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּאַחְרָיוּת נָמֵי!

a8.he: לָא, דִּלְמָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כַּאֲבוּהּ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת.

a9.he: תְּנַן: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת צִבּוּר מֵתָה, הָא דְּיָחִיד מֵתָה.

a10.he: אָמַר רַב: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּין אֵינָן נִידְחִין, כְּשֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֵׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג רִאשׁוֹן מִתְכַּפֵּר, וְאִידַּךְ הָוֵה לֵיהּ אַחְרָיוּת, וְקָתָנֵי דְּיָחִיד מֵתָה!

a12.he: תָּנֵי רַב שִׁימִי בַּר זֵירִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא: אָבְדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה — לְרַבִּי מֵתָה, לְרַבָּנַן תִּרְעֶה. אָבְדָה בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה — לְרַבָּנַן מֵתָה, לְרַבִּי רוֹעֶה.

a13.he: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה, דְּאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן רוֹעָה, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵתָה — אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה, דִּלְרַבָּנַן מֵתָה, לְרַבִּי לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

a14.he: אֶלָּא תָּנֵי הָכִי: אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה — לְרַבִּי מֵתָה, לְרַבָּנַן רוֹעָה. בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מֵתָה.

a15.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.

a16.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב, כְּיוֹצֵא בוֹ — אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בִּבְכוֹר, וְלֹא בִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין.

a17.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב — דְּקָא טָרַח טִירְחָא דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ, אֶלָּא בְּכוֹר — מַאן תְּנָא?

a18.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא, דְּאָמַר: בְּכוֹר בִּקְדוּשְּׁתֵיהּ קָאֵי, דִּתְנַן: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: לֹא יִמָּנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַכֹּהֵן עַל הַבְּכוֹר.

a19.he: פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי חַטָּאוֹת, אַחַת תְּמִימָה וְאַחַת בַּעֲלַת מוּם — תְּמִימָה תִּקְרַב, בַּעֲלַת מוּם תִּפָּדֶה.

a20.he: נִשְׁחֲטָה בַּעֲלַת מוּם, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — מוּתֶּרֶת; מִשֶּׁנִּזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — אֲסוּרָה.

a21.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׂר בַּעֲלַת מוּם בַּקְּדֵירָה, וְנִזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — יוֹצֵא לְבֵית הַשְׂרֵיפָה.

a22.he: וְרַב חִסְדָּא, לוֹקְמַהּ אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי!

a23.he: דִּלְמָא כִּי אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי — בִּבְכוֹר, דִּקְדוּשְּׁתֵיהּ מֵרֶחֶם, אֲבָל פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין — לָא.

a24.he: וְלוֹקְמַאּ אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן!

a25.he: דִּלְמָא כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — בִּפְסוּלֵי מוּקְדָּשִׁין, דְּאַלִּימִי לְמִיתְפַּס פִּדְיוֹנָן, אֲבָל בִּבְכוֹר — לָא.

a26.he: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לֵית לֵיהּ הָא דִּתְנַן: כׇּל פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין נִשְׁחָטִין בָּאִיטְלִיז וְנִמְכָּרִין בָּאִיטְלִיז וְנִשְׁקָלִין בְּלִיטְרָא? אַלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁרֵית לֵיהּ טָפֵי וְזָבֵין!

a27.he: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: מַה שֶׁמַּשְׁבִּיחַ בָּעוֹר — פּוֹגֵם בְּבָשָׂר.

a28.he: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה בְּקָדָשִׁים.

a29.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְגַדֵּל מֵהֶם עֲדָרִים עֲדָרִים.

b1.he: מַתְנִי׳ כֵּיצַד מַעֲרִימִין עַל הַבְּכוֹר? מְבַכֶּרֶת שֶׁהָיְתָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת, אוֹמֵר: ״מַה שֶּׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל זוֹ אִם זָכָר — עוֹלָה״, יָלְדָה זָכָר — יִקְרַב עוֹלָה, ״וְאִם נְקֵבָה — זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים״, יָלְדָה נְקֵבָה — תִּקְרַב שְׁלָמִים.

b2.he: ״אִם זָכָר — עוֹלָה, וְאִם נְקֵבָה — זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים״, יָלְדָה זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — הַזָּכָר יִקְרַב עוֹלָה, וְהַנְּקֵבָה תִּקְרַב שְׁלָמִים. יָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים — אֶחָד מֵהֶם יִקְרַב עוֹלָה, וְהַשֵּׁנִי יִמָּכֵר לְחַיָּיבֵי עוֹלָה, וְדָמָיו חוּלִּין.

b3.he: יָלְדָה שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת — אַחַת מֵהֶם תִּקְרַב שְׁלָמִים, וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה תִּימָּכֵר לְחַיָּיבֵי שְׁלָמִים, וְדָמֶיהָ חוּלִּין. יָלְדָה טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֵין קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עֲלֵיהֶן.

b4.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מוּתָּר לְהַטִּיל מוּם בִּבְכוֹר קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֵּצֵא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם. תְּנַן: אוֹמֵר אָדָם ״מַה שֶּׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה״ — עוֹלָה אִין, שְׁלָמִים לָא, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ דְּמָצֵית מַפְקְעַתְּ לֵיהּ מִקְּדוּשְּׁתַהּ!

b5.he: אָמַר לָךְ רַב יְהוּדָה: הָנֵי מִילֵּי — בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, כִּי קָאָמֵינָא אֲנָא — בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, דְּלָא חֲזֵי לְהַקְרָבָה.

b6.he: אִי בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא? מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: נִגְזַר, דִּלְמָא נָפֵיק רוֹב רֹאשׁוֹ וְקָשָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא.

b7.he: וְאֵימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי! אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי — הָא עֲדִיפָא יַתִּירָא, מִדְּאָתֵי בֵּיהּ לִידֵי גִּיזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה.

b8.he: אִם נְקֵבָה זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים — נְקֵבָה מִי קָא קָדְשָׁה בִּבְכוֹרָה? סֵיפָא אָתְיָא לִבְהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ.

b9.he: יָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים כּוּ׳. אָמְרִי: אִי בְּהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ, הַיְאךְ דְּאַקְדֵּישׁ עוֹלָה — לֶיהְדַּר עוֹלָה, אִידַּךְ נֶהֱוֵי בִּקְדוּשְּׁתַיהּ דְּאִימֵּיהּ! סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְבֶהֱמַת חוּלִּין.

messages.text: Continued from 23b: Rabbi Ami taught that one who designates two piles of money as a guarantee for his sin offering achieves atonement with one, and the second goes to communal gift offerings. The Gemara explained that this is needed according to Rabbi Shimon: one might have thought that he allows gift offerings only from a surplus in one set of money,

But in a case where one designates two distinct sets of money, such as an additional set of money as a guarantee, Rabbi Shimon does not state that the surplus money is allocated for communal gift offerings. Rabbi Ami therefore teaches us that even in this case, Rabbi Shimon agrees that the surplus money is allocated for communal gift offerings.

notes.he: כגון הפריש שני צבורי מעות לאחריות ונתכפר בא' דדחי להו לאינך אימא לית ליה:
notes.en: But with two sets: for example, he set aside two piles of money as a guarantee and achieved atonement with one, so that the other is pushed aside; one might say that he [Rabbi Shimon] does not hold [that it goes to gift offerings].

notes.he: ר' אמי:
notes.en: It teaches us: [that is,] Rabbi Ami [teaches us].

notes.he: היינו ב' צבורין ונותר אחד מהן לית ליה:
notes.en: But with two sets: that is, two piles, and one of them is left over; he [Rabbi Shimon] does not hold [that it goes to gift offerings].

notes.he: ר' אמי דאית ליה:
notes.en: It teaches us: Rabbi Ami, who holds [that even Rabbi Shimon allows it].

messages.text: In the case of one who designates two animals as sin offerings as a guarantee, so that if one animal is lost he will achieve atonement with the other animal, he achieves atonement with one of them, and the other is left to graze until it develops a blemish. It is then sold, and the money received from its sale is used to purchase communal gift offerings.
In accordance with whose opinion does Rabbi Hoshaya state this halakha? If we say that it is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, then it is unnecessary.
messages.quote: he achieves atonement with one of them, and the other is left to graze

messages.text: Now that in a case where one designates a sin offering instead of one that was lost, the Rabbis say that it is not considered like the lost animal, and it is therefore left to graze, is it necessary to state that in a case where one designates an additional sin offering as a guarantee, the second animal is left to graze?

notes.he: דהכא ליכא אבודה:
notes.en: One who designates as a guarantee, is it necessary [to say] that it grazes? For here there is no lost animal at all.

messages.text: Rather, you will say that Rabbi Hoshaya states this halakha in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon. But didn’t Rabbi Shimon say that there are five sin offerings that are left to die, one of which is a sin offering whose owner has achieved atonement with another animal? If so, even in a case where one designated an additional animal as a guarantee, once the owner has achieved atonement the remaining animal is left to die.

notes.he: בכל ענין שהן והך חדא מינייהו היא שכיפרו בעליה:
notes.en: Five sin offerings die: in every circumstance in which they occur; and this is one of them, [a sin offering] whose owner has achieved atonement.

notes.he: אלא אליבא דר' שמעון הא אמר חמש חטאות מתות והאחת מהן חטאת שכפרו בעלים והכא ליכא למימר והא אית ליה לר' שמעון נדבה דאמרינן כי אית ליה הני מילי במותר מעות חטאת אבל הכא דחטאת עצמו נותרה לר"ש ודאי מתה:
notes.en: Rather, according to Rabbi Shimon? But he said that five sin offerings die, and one of them is a sin offering whose owner has achieved atonement. And here one cannot say: but Rabbi Shimon does hold [that surplus goes to] gift offerings! For we said that when he holds so, that applies only to the surplus money of a sin offering; but here, where the sin offering itself is left over, according to Rabbi Shimon it certainly dies.

messages.text: Rather, Rabbi Hoshaya states this halakha in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. Rabbi Hoshaya is teaching that when Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said that a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another animal is left to die, that applies only in a case where one designated the second animal instead of a lost sin offering. But in a case where one initially designated an additional sin offering as a guarantee, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi does not hold that the remaining offering is left to die.

notes.he: קאמר רועה דכי אמר רבי מתה באבודה אבל באחריות ההיא דנותרה רועה:
notes.en: Rather, according to Rabbi: he says it grazes; for when Rabbi said “it dies,” that was with a lost animal, but with a guarantee, the one that is left over grazes.

messages.text: We learned in the mishna (22b):
messages.quote: But in a case where one initially designated an additional sin offering as a guarantee

messages.text: In the case of one who designates a sin offering and the animal is blemished, he sells the animal and brings another sin offering in its stead with the money received in its sale.

If the second animal is sacrificed before the first is slaughtered for non-sacred consumption, the first animal shall be left to die, as it is considered an animal whose owner already achieved atonement with another animal.

It enters your mind to say that Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who says that if one achieved atonement with one sin offering, the remaining animal is left to die. Likewise, even if the remaining animal is no longer sacred, it is left to die if the owner achieved atonement with the other animal.

notes.he: דאמר אבודה בשעת הפרשה מתה משום כפרו בעליה [באחרת] וכי מפריש שניה לאחריות נמי יכפרו הבעלים באחרת והיא מתה לשון זה פשוט:
notes.en: He holds like Rabbi: who said that one lost at the time of designation dies, because its owner achieved atonement [with another]. And when one designates a second as a guarantee, the owner will also achieve atonement with another, and it dies. This version is straightforward.

notes.he: דמחמיר ואמר מפריש לאבוד כאבוד דמי וש"מ דאפילו היכא דליכא אבוד כגון הכא דלא אבדה הראשונה אלא באחריות שכשהוממה הראשונה הפריש אותה הכי ואפ"ה מתה:
notes.en: He holds like Rabbi: who is stringent and says that one who designates [a replacement] for a lost animal, it is considered as lost. And learn from it that even where there is no loss, as here, where the first was not lost but [the second stood] as a guarantee, for when the first became blemished he designated that one in this way, and even so it dies.

notes.dh: ר' אלעזר ב"ר שמעון אומר אם קרבה שניה
notes.he: שהביא בדמיה עד שלא נשחטה הראשונה תמות אע"ג שיצא לחולין קס"ד דר' אלעזר ב"ר שמעון כרבי סבירא ליה ומש"ה קאמר קס"ד דכרבי ס"ל משום דר' אושעיא אליבא דרבי קאמר ובעי לאקשויי ליה מרבי דאמר אחת מהן תקרב והשני תמות דכי היכי דסבירא ליה לר' במפריש חטאתו ואבדה הכי נמי סבירא ליה לרבי אפילו (במוכר לאחרים) [במפרשן לאחריות] שכבר כפרו בעלים וכיון דבהא דחולין היא אפ"ה א"ר אלעזר בר"ש הראשונה תמות כ"ש [דאפילו באחריות] היכא דאיפריש ב' חטאות לאחריות דתרוייהו אית להו שם חטאת עליהם שאם נתכפר באחת שחברתה מתה וקשיא לר' אושעיא:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: If the second, which he brought with its money, was sacrificed before the first was slaughtered, it dies, even though it has gone out to non-sacred status. “It enters your mind that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi”: and why does it say “it enters your mind that he holds like Rabbi”? Because Rabbi Oshaya spoke according to Rabbi, and it wants to challenge him from Rabbi, who said that one of them is sacrificed and the second dies. Just as Rabbi holds so for one who designated his sin offering and it was lost, so too Rabbi holds even [for one who designates them as a guarantee; the edition corrects the text to read so], since the owner has already achieved atonement. And since even in this case, where it is non-sacred, Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says that the first dies, all the more so [even with a guarantee], where one designated two sin offerings as a guarantee and both bear the name of a sin offering: if he achieved atonement with one, its partner dies. And this is difficult for Rabbi Oshaya.

messages.text: And if so, even if one initially designated an additional sin offering as a guarantee, the remaining animal should also be left to die. Consequently, the statement of Rabbi Hoshaya cannot be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

notes.he: והא הכא ליכא למימר מצוה בראשון להכי שניה מתה אלא הכא אפילו ראשונה מתה אלמא אלימא קדושת דמים (הא) [דהאי] בעלת מום דלית בה אלא קדושת דמים נדחית ואע"ג דנפדית מתה מאי לאו אפילו רבי דאמר והשניה תמות סבר ליה נמי בהא דמתה וכ"ש באחריות לא:
notes.en: Another version: but here one cannot say “it is a mitzva with the first, and that is why the second dies”; rather, here even the first dies. Apparently monetary sanctity is strong, for this blemished animal, which has only monetary sanctity, is rejected, and even though it was redeemed it dies. Is it not that even Rabbi, who said “and the second dies,” holds that in this case it dies, and all the more so [it would die] with a guarantee?

messages.text: No, perhaps Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, does not hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. Rather, he holds in accordance with the opinion of his father, Rabbi Shimon, who said that there are five sin offerings left to die, one of which is a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another animal.

notes.dh: כאבוה סבירא ליה דאמר חמש חטאות מתות
notes.he: בכל ענין שהן:
notes.en: He holds like his father, who said five sin offerings die: in every circumstance in which they occur.

notes.he: ר' אלעזר בר"ש כאבוה (ר' שמעון) ס"ל דאמר חמש חטאות מתות כו'. וחטאת שכפרו בעלים [בכלל] ואנא לא אמרי אליבא דר"ש אלא אליבא דרבי:
notes.en: He [Rabbi Oshaya] can say to you: No, perhaps Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds like his father, who said five sin offerings die, etc., and a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement is [among them]; and I did not speak according to Rabbi Shimon but according to Rabbi.

notes.he: לא סבר לה כרבי בהא אלא ר' אלעזר בר"ש סבירא ליה כאבוה כדאמרן:
notes.en: He does not hold like Rabbi in this; rather, Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds like his father, as we said.

messages.text: Since Rabbi Shimon does not qualify this statement, he evidently maintains that the remaining sin offering is always left to die, even when it is no longer sacred. If so, the statement of Rabbi Hoshaya can be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
We learned in a mishna (Yoma 62a):
messages.quote: he achieves atonement with one of them, and the other is left to graze

messages.text: With regard to the lottery involving the two goats brought on Yom Kippur, if after the lots were drawn for both goats, the scapegoat died, another pair of goats is brought and lots are drawn for the second pair. With regard to the two goats selected to be the sin offering, i.e., the remaining goat from the first pair and the goat selected from the second, one is sacrificed and the second goat shall graze until it becomes blemished, after which it is sold and the money received is allocated for communal gift offerings. This is because a communal sin offering is not left to die.

notes.he: אשעירי יוה"כ קאי:
notes.en: Because a communal sin offering does not die: this refers to the goats of Yom Kippur.

messages.text: One may infer from the mishna that under similar circumstances, the sin offering of an individual is left to die.

Living animals are not rejected. In other words, the sin offering from the first pair is not disqualified on account of the death of the first scapegoat. And therefore, when he achieves atonement, he may achieve atonement even with the second goat of the first pair.
messages.lead: And as the mishna does not specify which of the two goats is brought as the sin offering,

notes.he: ולא נדחה הראשון במיתת חבירו וכשהוא מתכפר אם ירצה יתכפר בשני שבזוג ראשון ואידך בתרא כמפרישו לאחריות כלו' שלא הופרש תחת אבוד שהרי לא מת מזוג ראשון אלא שעיר של עזאזל ולא של שם ואפ"ה מתה וקשיא לר' אושעיא:
notes.en: Living animals are not rejected: and the first [goat] is not rejected by the death of its partner. And when he achieves atonement, if he wishes, he may achieve atonement with the second of the first pair; and the other one, the latter, is like one he designated as a guarantee, that is, it was not designated in place of a lost one, since from the first pair only the goat for Azazel died, not the one for the Name. And even so it dies, and this is difficult for Rabbi Oshaya [the daf: Rabbi Hoshaya].

messages.text: And the other goat that was selected as the sin offering from the second pair is like one that was initially consecrated as a guarantee, as it was not consecrated to replace a lost offering. And yet the mishna teaches that in a comparable case involving the sin offering of an individual, it is left to die. This apparently contradicts the ruling of Rabbi Hoshaya.

notes.dh: ואידך הוה ליה לאחריות וקתני הא דיחיד מתה
notes.he: וא"ת לעיל פריך מהא לר' אבא דחשיב ליה כמפריש לאיבוד והכא חשיב ליה כמפריש לאחריות וי"ל דמשתמע ליה השתא כיון דבשעה שהפריש השני היה יודע שלא יתכפר בו אלא בשני שבזוג ראשון ה"ל באחריות ולא דמי להפריש לאיבוד דלעיל דהתם היה סובר דהראשון נאבד ומתכפר בזה שמפריש עתה והוה ליה כמפריש לאיבוד ולא הוי באחריות אבל הכא שהיה יודע בשעת הפרשת השני שיתכפר בראשון הוה ליה כמו אחריות ואפ"ה קאמר דיחיד מתה וקשה לרבי אושעיא דאמר מפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות מתכפר באחת מהן והשני רועה ומשני רב לטעמיה דאמר מצוה בראשון ומשעה שהופרש הופרש לאיבוד ואין זה אחריות ולכך מתה והא דמדמי ליה לעיל למפריש לאיבוד היינו מטעם דמצותו בראשון או שמא יש לפרש דס"ל הכא כרב הונא דאמר לעיל אינה אבודה אינה מתה לא לרבי ולא לרבנן ומשום הכי פריך מינה דהיה סבור שהוא כמפריש לאחריות:
notes.en: And the other is a guarantee, and it teaches that an individual’s dies: And if you say: above, the Gemara challenged Rabbi Abba from this very case, treating it as one who designates for a lost animal, while here it treats it as one who designates as a guarantee? One can say: now it understands that since, at the time he designated the second, he knew that he would achieve atonement not with it but with the second of the first pair, it is a guarantee. It is unlike the designation for a lost animal above, for there he thought the first was lost and that he would achieve atonement with the one he was now designating, so it was like designating for a lost animal and not a guarantee. But here, since he knew at the time he designated the second that he would achieve atonement with the first, it is like a guarantee; and even so it says that an individual’s dies. And this is difficult for Rabbi Oshaya, who said that one who designates two sin offerings as a guarantee achieves atonement with one of them and the second grazes. And it answers: Rav conforms to his reasoning, as he said it is a mitzva with the first, so from the moment it was designated it was designated for loss, and this is not a guarantee, and therefore it dies. And what [the Gemara] compared it to above, to one who designates for a lost animal, was for the reason that the mitzva is with the first. Or perhaps one can explain that here it holds like Rav Huna, who said above that if it is not lost it does not die, neither according to Rabbi nor according to the Rabbis; and that is why it challenged from it, since it thought it was like one who designates as a guarantee.

notes.he: הוה ליה לאחריות שאם יאבד שני שבזוג ראשון יקרב זה תחתיו וקתני הא דיחיד מתה וקשיא לר' אושעיא דאמר חברתה רועה אמר לך ר' אושעיא רב אומר בעלי חיין (הן) [אינן] נדחין וכשהוא מתכפר כו'. סבר לה כר' יוסי דאמר לענין פסח מצוה בראשון הכא נמי מצוה בראשון והוה ליה אידך שני שבזוג שני מופרש לאיבוד וכל מופרש לאיבוד כאבוד דמי:
notes.en: And the other, the second of the second pair, is a guarantee: for if the second of the first pair is lost, this one is sacrificed in its stead; and it teaches that an individual’s dies. This is difficult for Rabbi Oshaya, who said its partner grazes. Rabbi Oshaya can say to you: Rav says living animals are not rejected, and when he achieves atonement, etc. He [Rav] holds like Rabbi Yosei, who said with regard to the Paschal offering that it is a mitzva with the first. Here too it is a mitzva with the first, and so the other, the second of the second pair, was designated for loss, and anything designated for loss is considered as lost.

messages.text: Rav conforms to his standard line of reasoning, as he said: It is a mitzva to sacrifice the first offering that was designated.
messages.quote: And the other goat that was selected as the sin offering from the second pair is like one that was initially consecrated as a guarantee

notes.he: כרבי יוסי דאמר מצוה בראשון דקתני גבי פסחים הפריש פסחו ואבד והפריש אחר תחתיו ונמצא הראשון איזה שירצה יקריב ר' יוסי אומר מצוה בראשון ורב סבר לה כוותיה וכיון דמצוה בראשון הוה ליה מפריש לאיבוד תחלת הפרשתו של שני לא היתה לשם הקדש אלא (לשם) כדי שיאבד וילך למיתה הואיל דס"ל מצוה בראשון אבל גבי שתי חטאות לאחריות כיון דאי הוה בעי מתכפר בהאי דשייך ליכא למימר תחלת הפרשה לאיבוד:
notes.en: Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei, who said it is a mitzva with the first, as is taught about Paschal offerings: One designated his Paschal offering and it was lost, and he designated another in its stead, and then the first was found; he may sacrifice whichever he wishes. Rabbi Yosei says: it is a mitzva with the first. And Rav holds like him. And since it is a mitzva with the first, it is like one who designates for a lost animal: the second was designated at the outset not for the sake of consecration but so that it would be lost and go to its death, since he holds it is a mitzva with the first. But with two sin offerings as a guarantee, since if he wished he could achieve atonement with this one, which is fitting, one cannot say that it was designated at the outset for loss.

messages.text: Consequently, when the second sin offering is consecrated, it is already known that it will not be sacrificed. It is therefore considered like an animal designated instead of one that was lost. But in a case where one initially designates an additional sin offering as a guarantee, he is permitted to achieve atonement with either animal ab initio. Therefore, the one that is not sacrificed is left to graze.

notes.he: והיכא אמר ר' תמות באבוד אבל באחריות דליכא אבוד לא א"ר הלכך הא דיחיד תמות כר' יוסי ולי לא סבירא לי]:
notes.en: [Continuing Rabbi Oshaya’s answer:] And where did Rabbi say “it dies”? With a lost animal; but with a guarantee, where there is no lost animal, Rabbi did not say so. Therefore this ruling, that an individual’s dies, follows Rabbi Yosei, and I do not hold so.

messages.text: In a case where a sin offering was lost at the time when one designated a sin offering in its stead, and one found the lost sin offering before sacrificing the replacement, there is a dispute between tanna’im. According to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, the offering that is not sacrificed is left to die, and according to the Rabbis it shall be left to graze.
messages.lead: § With regard to the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and the Rabbis, Rav Shimi bar Ziri taught the following baraita before Rav Pappa:

messages.text: If the first sin offering was lost at the time when one achieved atonement with another animal, then according to the Rabbis the first sin offering is left to die, and according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi it is left to graze.

This cannot be correct, due to an a fortiori inference: And what, if in the case of a sin offering that was lost at the time when its owner designated an animal in its stead, where the Rabbis say that the offering that is not sacrificed is left to graze, and yet Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says it is left to die, then in the case of a sin offering that was lost at the time when its owner achieved atonement with another animal, where according to the Rabbis the remaining animal is left to die, is it not all the more so true that according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi it is left to die?
messages.lead: Rav Pappa said to Rav Shimi bar Ziri:
messages.quote: according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi it is left to graze

messages.text: Rather, teach the baraita in this manner: If a sin offering was lost at the time when one designated an animal in its stead, and the owner found the lost sin offering before sacrificing the replacement, according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi the offering that is not sacrificed is left to die, and according to the Rabbis it is left to graze.
If the first sin offering was lost at the time when one achieved atonement with another animal, all agree that it is left to die.

messages.caption: Rav Shimi bar Ziri’s baraita as he taught it, and as the Gemara teaches it after Rav Pappa’s a fortiori.

messages.text: If the second animal is sacrificed before the first is slaughtered for non-sacred consumption, the first animal shall be left to die. Although it was sold and rendered non-sacred, its status is that of a sin offering whose owner already achieved atonement with another animal.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches: In the case of one who designates a sin offering and the animal is blemished, he sells the animal and must bring another sin offering with the money received from its sale.

messages.text: One may not flay the skin of an animal from its feet on a Festival. Although it is permitted to slaughter and skin an animal on a Festival, one may not do so in such a manner to retain the hide intact to enable it to function as a vessel, e.g., a water skin.

notes.he: כדרך שמתחילין להפשיט העור דרך הרגלים והופכו שלם לצורך נפחים או לצורך דבש ושאינו רוצה להפשיטו שלם כשמפשיטו בסכין דרך בטנו מגרונו עד זנבו:
notes.en: One may not flay a firstborn from its feet: the way one begins to strip the hide by way of the legs and turns it inside out whole, for the needs of smiths [for bellows] or for honey; as opposed to one who does not want to strip it whole, who strips it with a knife along its belly, from its throat to its tail.

notes.he: ביו"ט לפשוט עור בהמה שלם לצורך מפוח ולהכי קרי ליה מרגילין דדרך הרגלים מתחילין לפשוט עור לשום אותו צורך וביו"ט אסור דקא טרח ביה טרחא יתירא:
notes.en: One may not flay from the feet: on a Festival, stripping the hide of an animal whole for the needs of a bellows. It is called margilin because for that purpose one begins stripping the hide by way of the legs [raglayim]. And on a Festival it is prohibited, since one exerts excessive effort.

messages.text: Similarly, one may not flay a firstborn kosher animal from its feet even on a weekday, and even if the animal is blemished, nor may one flay from the feet disqualified consecrated animals that have been redeemed, as flaying from the feet is considered degrading.

notes.he: שנפדו ושחטן:
notes.en: Nor with disqualified consecrated animals: that were redeemed and he slaughtered them.

messages.text: Granted, everyone agrees that one may not flay an animal from its feet on a Festival, as one who does so exerts effort that is not fit for the Festival. But with regard to a firstborn offering, who is the tanna who taught that flaying from its feet is prohibited?
messages.quote: Similarly, one may not flay a firstborn kosher animal from its feet

messages.text: It is the opinion of Beit Shammai, who say that a firstborn animal retains its sanctity even after it becomes blemished. As we learned in a mishna (Bekhorot 32b) that
Beit Shammai say: An Israelite may not be granted a portion of a blemished firstborn animal along with a priest.

notes.he: לאכול עם הכהן בשר בכור בעל מום ששחטו כהן. אלמא אף על גב דהומם בקדושתיה קאי הלכך אין מרגילין בו דדמי כעבודה בקדשים וכעובדין דחולין:
notes.en: An Israelite may not be counted with the priest: to eat with the priest the meat of a blemished firstborn that a priest slaughtered. Apparently, even though it became blemished, it retains its sanctity; therefore one may not flay it from the feet, since that resembles labor with sacred animals and the practices of non-sacred ones.

messages.text: Just as Beit Shammai prohibit an Israelite from partaking of even a blemished firstborn animal, they prohibit flaying the skin of a firstborn animal from its feet.
With regard to disqualified consecrated animals, who is the tanna who taught that one may not flay them from their feet?
messages.quote: nor may one flay from the feet disqualified consecrated animals

messages.text: It is the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon. As it is taught in a baraita:

If there were two sin offerings before him, where one was designated as a guarantee for the other should it become lost or disqualified, and one was unblemished and one became blemished after it was designated, then the unblemished animal shall be sacrificed and the blemished animal shall be redeemed.

notes.he: קודם הפרשת השניה והנך שתי חטאות לשם חטא אחד הופרשו שנפל מום בראשונה והפריש שניה תחתיה:
notes.en: The blemished one shall be redeemed: before the designation of the second. And these two sin offerings were designated for a single sin: a blemish befell the first and he designated the second in its stead.

messages.text: If the blemished animal was slaughtered after it was redeemed, and this occurred before the blood of the unblemished animal was sprinkled upon the altar, then the meat of the blemished animal is permitted. But if it was slaughtered after the blood of the unblemished animal was sprinkled on the altar, it is prohibited to derive benefit from the blemished animal, as it has the status of a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another animal.

notes.he: לאחר פדיונה:
notes.en: The blemished one was slaughtered: after its redemption.

notes.he: דהואי חטאת שכיפרו בעליה:
notes.en: Prohibited: since it is a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement.

messages.text: Even if the meat of the blemished animal is already cooking in the pot, and the blood of the unblemished sin offering was then sprinkled on the altar, it is prohibited to derive benefit from the meat of the blemished animal, and it goes to the place designated for burning disqualified offerings, as it is considered a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another animal.

notes.he: את בשר הבעלת מום. אלמא אע"ג דאיפריק ואישתחיט בקדושתה קיימא וחטאת שכיפרו הבעלים מיקרייא הלכך גבי הרגלה נמי אע"ג דאיפריק ואישתחיט בקדושתה קיימא:
notes.en: Goes out to the place of burning: the meat of the blemished one. Apparently, even though it was redeemed and slaughtered, it retains its sanctity and is called a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement. Therefore, with regard to flaying from the feet too, even though it was redeemed and slaughtered, it retains its sanctity.

notes.dh: רבי אלעזר בר' שמעון אומר אפילו בשר בעלת מום בקדירה כו'
notes.he: וא"ת מ"ש הכא ממתני' דאמרי רבנן בההיא דמתני' דאפילו נזרק דמה דשניה בעוד ראשונה בעלת מום קיימא אין לה דין מיתה והכא אמר דאם נשחטה בעלת מום משנזרק דם תמימה אסורה ולר' אלעזר בר' שמעון אפילו בשר בקדירה כשנזרק דמה של תמימה תצא לבית השריפה ובמתני' קאמר דאם נשחטה בעלת מום קודם זריקת דמה של תמימה דכשרה ויש לחלק דבההיא דמתני' כיון דהיתה כבר בעלת מום קודם הפרשה של זו אין עליה קדושה כל כך אבל הכא דהופרשו לאחריות ונראו שניהם להקריב עליה קדושה יותר:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: even the meat of the blemished one in the pot, etc.: And if you say: how is this different from our mishna [22b]? There the Rabbis say that even if the blood of the second was sprinkled while the first, the blemished one, still exists, it is not subject to death; yet here it says that if the blemished one was slaughtered after the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled, it is prohibited, and according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, even if the meat is in the pot when the blood of the unblemished one is sprinkled, it goes out to the place of burning; while in the mishna he says that if the blemished one was slaughtered before the sprinkling of the unblemished one’s blood, it is fit. One can distinguish: in the case of the mishna, since it was already blemished before the other was designated, it does not carry so much sanctity; but here, where they were designated as a guarantee and both appeared fit to be sacrificed, it carries more sanctity.

notes.he: אפילו נשחטה בעלת מום קודם זריקת דם של תמימה ובשר בעלת מום בקדירה ונזרק דמה של תמימה קודם שנאכל הבשר של בעלת מום תצא לבית השרפה אלמא לר"א בר"ש אע"ג דשחטה לבעלת מום דהיינו פסולי המוקדשין בקדושה קאי אע"ג דנפדה אי נזרק דמה של תמימה קודם אכילתו תצא לבית השרפה:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: even if the blemished one was slaughtered before the sprinkling of the unblemished one’s blood, and the meat of the blemished one is in the pot, and the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled before the meat of the blemished one was eaten, it goes out to the place of burning. Apparently, according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, even though he slaughtered the blemished one, which is [one of the] disqualified consecrated animals, it retains its sanctity though it was redeemed: if the blood of the unblemished one was sprinkled before it was eaten, it goes out to the place of burning.

messages.text: Just as Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, prohibits the meat of a disqualified sin offering that was redeemed and slaughtered, he likewise prohibits one from flaying it from its feet.

And let Rav Ḥisda establish both this halakha and that halakha in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai. Why does Rav Ḥisda establish the prohibition against flaying disqualified consecrated animals from the feet specifically in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon? Presumably, just as Beit Shammai prohibit flaying a firstborn from its feet, they also prohibit one from doing so to disqualified consecrated animals.

notes.he: דודאי כי היכי דמחמרי ב"ש בבכור מחמרי נמי בשאר פסולי המוקדשין מ"ש דאוקים רישא כב"ש וסיפא כרבי [אלעזר ברבי שמעון]:
notes.en: Both as Beit Shammai: for surely, just as Beit Shammai are stringent with a firstborn, they are also stringent with other disqualified consecrated animals. Why did he establish the first clause as Beit Shammai and the latter clause as Rabbi [Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon]?

notes.he: לבכור ולפסולי המוקדשין כב"ש ונימא כי היכי דסבירא להו בבכור דאע"ג דשחטיה בקדושה קאי ואין נוהגין בו בזיון להרגילן הכי נמי סבירא להו בפסולי המוקדשין:
notes.en: And let him establish both: the firstborn and the disqualified consecrated animals, as Beit Shammai; and say that just as they hold for a firstborn that even though he slaughtered it, it retains its sanctity and one does not treat it with disgrace by flaying it from the feet, so too they hold for disqualified consecrated animals.

messages.text: Perhaps when Beit Shammai said that a firstborn animal retains its sanctity even after it is blemished, they said that only with regard to a firstborn, whose sanctity is attained from the womb, i.e., from birth. But with regard to disqualified consecrated animals, perhaps Beit Shammai do not hold that they retain their sanctity after they become blemished and are redeemed.

But let Rav Ḥisda establish both this halakha and that halakha in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon. Presumably, just as Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, prohibits one from flaying disqualified consecrated animals from the feet, he also prohibits one from doing so to firstborn animals.

Perhaps when Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, said that the sanctity of a blemished consecrated animal remains even if it was already redeemed and is cooking in the pot, he said this only with regard to disqualified consecrated animals, whose sanctity is strong enough to apply to the redemption money paid for these animals. But in the case of a blemished firstborn animal, which cannot be redeemed, Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, does not hold that it retains its sanctity even after it is blemished.

notes.he: בכור אין לו פדיון דכתיב (במדבר יח) לא תפדה ואם פדאו אינו תופס פדיונו בקדושתו:
notes.en: A firstborn has no redemption, as it is written: “You shall not redeem” (Numbers 18:17); and if one redeemed it, its redemption money does not take on its sanctity.

notes.dh: דלמא ע"כ לא קאמר ב"ש כו'
notes.he: אלא בפסולי המוקדשין דאלימי למיתפס פדיונן שקדושתן על פדיונו והן יוצאין לחולין אבל בכור לא דכתיב ביה לא תפדה:
notes.en: Perhaps Beit Shammai said so only, etc. [The comment then gives the reasoning of the Gemara’s answer about Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:] only with disqualified consecrated animals, which are strong enough to take hold of their redemption, for their sanctity [passes] onto its redemption and they go out to non-sacred status; but not a firstborn, of which it is written: “You shall not redeem.”

messages.text: But does Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, not hold in accordance with that which we learned in a mishna (Bekhorot 31a):

All disqualified consecrated animals that have been redeemed may be slaughtered in the butchers’ market and sold in the butchers’ market, where there are many buyers, and their meat is weighed by the litra, like non-sacred meat.

notes.he: אלמא לאו בקדושתייהו קיימי מכי איפריק ואישתחיט:
notes.en: Slaughtered in the butchers’ market: apparently they do not retain their sanctity once they have been redeemed and slaughtered.

messages.text: Apparently, once you permit the sale of disqualified consecrated meat in the manner of non-sacred meat, one may increase the sale price and sell it at a greater profit. Since the Temple treasury stands to gain from such a sale, it is permitted to handle the disqualified consecrated meat in the manner of non-sacred meat. Here, too, as an animal that may be flayed from its feet would be sold for a higher price, the flaying from the feet of disqualified consecrated animals should be permitted, as the Temple treasury stands to gain from that sale.

notes.he: למוכרו באיטליז טפי ופריק ליה מיד הקדש ביוקר הואיל וסופו למוכרו יפה גבי הרגלה נמי לישתרי ליה להרגיל דכיון דידע בשעת פדיון דפסולי המוקדשין דסופו להרגיל ולמכור העור בדמים יקרים טפי ופריק ליה מיד הקדש:
notes.en: Apparently, since you permitted him: to sell it in the market, he adds and redeems it from the Temple treasury at a high price, since in the end he will sell it well. With flaying from the feet too, let him be permitted to flay; for since he knows at the time he redeems the disqualified consecrated animal that in the end he will flay it and sell the hide for a higher price, he will add and redeem it from the Temple treasury.

notes.he: ולית ליה לר"א בר"ש כל פסולי המוקדשין נמכרין באיטליז דנוהגין בזיון למוכרן בשוק מ"ט משום דכיון דשרית ליה לנהוג בהן כמו שירצה לשוקלן ולמוכרן בשוק מוסיף ופריק אותו ביוקר הכא נמי כיון דשרית ליה דמרגיל מוסיף ופודן ביוקר:
notes.en: And does Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon not hold that all disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the butchers’ market, which treats them with disgrace by selling them in the market? What is the reason [it is permitted]? Since you permitted him to treat them as he wishes, to weigh them and sell them in the market, he adds and redeems it at a high price. Here too, since you permitted him to flay it from the feet, he adds and redeems them at a high price.

messages.text: That which improves the hide damages the meat. If one is careful to remove the entire hide without cutting it, he will inevitably cut away some of the meat, thereby lowering the proceeds from the meat. Consequently, the ability to flay a disqualified consecrated animal from its feet does not increase its overall sale price.
messages.quote: the flaying from the feet of disqualified consecrated animals should be permitted

notes.he: מה שמשתכר בדמי העור פוגם בדמי הבשר ואין כאן ריוח לפי שמתירא לחתוך העור וחותך הבשר ושוב אינה יפה לימכר:
notes.en: What improves the hide damages the meat: what he gains in the price of the hide he loses in the price of the meat, and there is no profit here; for since he is afraid to cut the hide, he cuts the meat, and then it is no longer nice to sell.

notes.he: לית ליה לר' אלעזר הא מ"ט דמה שמשביח בעור פוגם בבשר הלכך לית ליה:
notes.en: Rav Mari said: [This is why] Rabbi Elazar does not hold this. What is the reason? What improves the hide damages the meat; therefore he does not hold it.

messages.text: It is because it appears as though one is performing labor with sacrificial animals, which is prohibited.
messages.lead: In the West, Eretz Yisrael, they said in the name of Rabbi Avin another reason it is prohibited to flay disqualified consecrated animals from their feet:

notes.he: שעושה מפוח על הבהמה בעודה מחובר ועבודה ממש ודאי לא הוי דאין עבודה לאחר מיתה אבל נראה כעבודה:
notes.en: Because it appears like one who performs labor with sacred animals: for he makes a bellows out of the animal while it is still whole. Actual labor it certainly is not, for there is no labor after death; but it looks like labor.

notes.he: במערבא אמרי מש"ה אסור דנרא' כעובד עבודה בקדשים:
notes.en: In the West they said: it is prohibited for this reason, that it looks like one who performs labor with sacred animals.

messages.text: The prohibition against flaying disqualified consecrated animals from the feet is a rabbinic decree, lest one delay slaughtering the animals until he finds someone to purchase the hide, and in doing so, he will raise many flocks of disqualified consecrated animals, which will likely lead to a transgression of the prohibitions of shearing or working disqualified consecrated animals.

notes.he: מפסולי המוקדשין:
notes.en: A decree lest he raise from them: from disqualified consecrated animals.

notes.he: דאי שרית ליה להרגיל משהי להו ולא שחיט עד שיזדמנו לו נפחים ואתי לגדל עדרים ואתי לידי תקלת גיזה ועבודה ופסולי המוקדשין אסורין בגיזה ועבודה אפילו לאחר פדיונן:
notes.en: Many flocks: for if you permit him to flay from the feet, he will keep them and not slaughter them until bellows-makers happen by, and he will come to raise flocks, and come to the stumbling block of shearing and work; and disqualified consecrated animals are prohibited for shearing and work even after their redemption.

notes.he: ור' יוסי בר אבין אמר מש"ה אסר דאי שרית להרגיל פעמים שאין מצויין שם נפחין שקונין העורות לצורך מפוחין ומשהין אותן ומגדלין מהן עדרים וגזירה שמא יבואו בהן לידי תקלה שיעבדו בהן הלכך גזרו דאין מרגילין בפסולי המוקדשין ולא אתו למישהינהו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said: he prohibited it for this reason: if you permit flaying from the feet, sometimes the bellows-makers, who buy hides for bellows, are not to be found there, and people would keep the animals and raise flocks from them. It is a decree lest they come to a stumbling block with them and work them. Therefore they decreed that one may not flay disqualified consecrated animals from the feet, so that people will not come to keep them.

notes.he: הדרן עלך ולד חטאת
notes.en: Hadran alakh Vlad Ḥatat: we will return to you, “The Offspring of a Sin Offering.”

Chapter 5 · כיצד מערימין · Keitzad Ma’arimin: how one may employ artifice with a firstborn, by consecrating the fetus for another offering while it is still in the womb.
Mishna
How may one employ artifice to circumvent the obligation to give the firstborn to the priest and utilize the animal for a different offering that he is obligated to bring?

notes.he: להפקיעו מכהן ולהפרישו לחובתו:
notes.en: Mishna. Employ artifice: to take it away from the priest and set it aside for his own obligation.

notes.he: מתני' כיצד מערימין:
notes.en: Mishna: How does one employ artifice. [Only the heading appears here; the comment follows in the next note.]

notes.he: דלא קדיש בכור עד דמקדיש ליה יציאת רחם אבל עד שהוא במעי אמו יכול לשנותו לדבר אחר:
notes.en: How does one employ artifice on the firstborn, etc.: for a firstborn is not sanctified until the opening of the womb sanctifies it; but while it is in its mother’s womb, he may change it to something else.

messages.text: The owner approaches an animal that is going to give birth to its firstborn while that animal was still pregnant, and says: That which is in the womb of this animal, if it is male, is designated as a burnt offering. In that case, if the animal gave birth to a male, it will be sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.he: דבכור לא קדיש אלא ברחם וכיון דמעיקרא אתפסיה בקדושה אחריתי תו לא חיילא קדושת בכורה:
notes.en: If it gave birth to a male, it shall be sacrificed as a burnt offering: for a firstborn becomes sacred only at [the opening of] the womb, and since he enclosed it in a different sanctity beforehand, the sanctity of a firstborn no longer takes effect.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ' דדוקא נקט עולה דלא נחתא מקדושתיה אבל שלמים לא דנחתא מקדושתייהו ואם נקבה זבחי שלמים בגמרא פריך ונקבה מי קא קדשה בבכורה. כלומר ול"ל להתפיסה בקדושה ומוקי לה בבהמת הקדש ואין רצונו שיחול עלה קדושת האם ורוצה להתפיסה בקדושה אחרת וסיפא דילדה שני זכרים מוקי לה בבהמה דחולין וא"כ מיירי רישא וסיפא בחולין ומציעתא בבהמת הקדש ותימה למורי הרמ"ר למה לא דחק לאוקומי מציעתא בבהמת חולין הרי סיפא דבחולין איירי ואפ"ה אתפיס בזבחי שלמים ותירץ משום דבעי לאוקומי אכיצד מערימין:
notes.en: If male, a burnt offering: it is explained in the Gemara that it says a burnt offering specifically, which does not lower its sanctity, but not peace offerings, which lower its sanctity. And on “if female, peace offerings,” the Gemara challenges: is a female sanctified as a firstborn? That is, he need not enclose it in a sanctity. And it establishes it with a consecrated animal, where he does not want the mother’s sanctity to take effect on it and wants to enclose it in a different sanctity. And the latter clause, “it gave birth to two males,” it establishes with a non-sacred animal; so the first clause and the latter clause concern non-sacred animals, and the middle clause a consecrated animal. My teacher, the RaMaR, found it difficult: why did it not strain to establish the middle clause with a non-sacred animal too? For the latter clause speaks of non-sacred animals, and even so he enclosed [the female] as peace offerings. And he answered: because it wants to fit it with “How does one employ artifice.”

messages.text: And in a case where he says: If it is female, it is designated as a peace offering, if the animal gave birth to a female, it will be sacrificed as a peace offering.

notes.he: אמר אם ילדה נקבה תהא זבחי שלמים ילדה נקבה תיקרב שלמים:
notes.en: And if: he said, “If it gives birth to a female, let it be a peace offering”; if it gave birth to a female, it is sacrificed as a peace offering.

messages.text: In a case where the owner says: If it is male it is designated as a burnt offering, and if it is female it is designated as a peace offering, and the animal gave birth to a male and a female, the male will be sacrificed as a burnt offering and the female will be sacrificed as a peace offering.

If the animal gave birth to two males, one of them will be sacrificed as a burnt offering and the second will be sold to those obligated to bring a burnt offering, who will sacrifice it as a burnt offering; and the money received from its sale is non-sacred.

notes.he: על שניהן חלה קדושת עולה דהא קאמר אם זכר יהא עולה ומיהו לא נדר אלא חד הלכך הוא יקריב האחד לנדרו והב' ימכר לצרכי עולה ודמיו חולין:
notes.en: If it gave birth to two males: the sanctity of a burnt offering takes effect on both of them, since he said “If male, let it be a burnt offering”; but he vowed only one. Therefore he sacrifices one for his vow, and the second is sold for the needs of a burnt offering, and its money is non-sacred.

notes.he: והשני ימכר לחייבי עולות ודמיו חולין משום הכי ימכר לחייבי עולות דילדה זכר סתם אם תהא עולה ועוד אין ידוע על איזה אמר הלכך שני ימכר לחייבי עולות [ומשום הכי] דמיו חולין דמ"מ לא הקדיש אלא אחד:
notes.en: And the second is sold to those obligated to bring burnt offerings, and its money is non-sacred: it is sold to those obligated to bring burnt offerings for this reason. (The edition notes that the text seems to need correcting, to read:) for he said “if male, a burnt offering” without specifying, and it is not known, etc.; that is, if it gave birth to a male, let it be a burnt offering, and moreover it is not known about which one he said it. Therefore the second is sold to those obligated to bring burnt offerings, [and for this reason] its money is non-sacred, for in any case he consecrated only one.

messages.text: If the animal gave birth to two females, one of them will be sacrificed as a peace offering and the second will be sold to those obligated to bring a peace offering, who will sacrifice it as a peace offering, and the money received from its sale is non-sacred.

notes.he: דינו כב' זכרים:
notes.en: It gave birth to two females: its law is as with two males.

messages.text: If the animal gave birth to a tumtum, whose gender is unknown, or a hermaphrodite, which has both male and female sexual organs, both of which are unfit for sacrifice,
They are not imbued with sanctity.
Gemara
It is permitted to inflict a blemish upon a firstborn before it left the womb and entered into the air of the world, as it has not yet become sanctified as a firstborn.

notes.dh: אמר רב יהודה מותר להטיל מום בבכור
notes.he: כדאמר בבכורות (דף לה.) גדיא באזניה אימרא בשיפוותיה וא"ת לימא דרב יהודה דהכא פליג אדרב הונא פרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף סט:) יצא שליש ומכרו לעובד כוכבים וחזר ויצא שליש אחר הרי זה קדוש בבכורה דכי נפק רובא לבסוף איגלאי מילתא למפרע דמעיקרא הוה קדיש ה"נ נימא גבי מטיל מום ויש לחלק בין מטיל מום למכירה דבמכירה יש לטעות יותר שמא ימכור אחר יציאת רובו:
notes.en: Rav Yehuda says: it is permitted to inflict a blemish on a firstborn: as it says in Bekhorot (35a): a kid by its ears, a lamb by its lips. And if you say: let us say that Rav Yehuda here disagrees with Rav Huna in chapter Behema HaMakshah (Ḥullin 69b): if a third emerged and he sold it to a gentile, and then another third emerged, it is sanctified as a firstborn, because when the majority emerged at the end it became clear retroactively that it was sanctified from the outset; here too let us say so for one who inflicts a blemish. One can distinguish between inflicting a blemish and selling: with selling there is more room to err, lest he sell after the majority has emerged.

notes.dh: מותר להטיל מום בבכור קודם שיצא לאויר העולם
notes.he: כגון אם יצא אזנו קודם או שפתו והטיל בה מום קודם שיצא רוב ראשו יקרב עולה:
notes.en: It is permitted to inflict a blemish on a firstborn before it emerges into the air of the world: for example, if its ear or its lip emerged first, and he inflicted a blemish on it before most of its head emerged, it is sacrificed as a burnt offering.

messages.text: We learned in the mishna: A person says about an animal that is going to give birth to its firstborn: That which is in the womb of this animal, if it is male, is designated as a burnt offering. This indicates that as a burnt offering, yes, one may designate it in this manner, as the sanctity of a burnt offering is more stringent than that of a firstborn but as a peace offering, no. And yet you say that one may entirely abrogate the animal’s sanctity by inflicting a blemish upon it before it is born.
messages.quote: It is permitted to inflict a blemish upon a firstborn before it left the womb

notes.he: הואיל וכליל היא שרי לשנויי קדושת בכורה לקדושתה אבל שלמים דקדושה קלה היא אסור לשנויי לכתחלה קדושת בכורה לקדושתייהו וכ"ש שאסור להטיל בו מום דמפיק ליה מקדושתיה לגמרי:
notes.en: Gemara. A burnt offering, yes: since it is burned entirely, one is permitted to change the firstborn’s sanctity to its sanctity; but peace offerings, which are of lesser sanctity, one may not change the firstborn’s sanctity to theirs ab initio; and all the more so it is prohibited to inflict a blemish on it, which takes it out of its sanctity entirely.

notes.he: כלומר לשם עולה דחמירה קדושתה מבכור יכול לשנותו אבל שלמים דגריע קדושה מבכור דנאכל לישראל לא יקרב וכ"ש להטיל מום דקא משוי ליה חולין דאסור:
notes.en: A burnt offering, yes: that is, to the status of a burnt offering, whose sanctity is more stringent than a firstborn’s, he may change it; but peace offerings, whose sanctity is lesser than a firstborn’s, since they are eaten by Israelites, it may not be sacrificed [as such]; and all the more so inflicting a blemish, which makes it non-sacred, is prohibited.

messages.text: That statement, that one is permitted to consecrate a firstborn fetus only with a more stringent sanctity, applies when the Temple is standing and offerings are sacrificed upon the altar. By contrast, when I say that one is permitted to inflict a blemish upon a firstborn and abrogate the firstborn’s sanctity, I am referring to today, when offerings are not able to be sacrificed, and therefore the animal cannot be consumed until it becomes blemished.

notes.he: מתני' דדייקינן מינה דלשם עולה אין לשם שלמים לא:
notes.en: Rav Yehuda holds: the mishna, from which we inferred “as a burnt offering, yes; as peace offerings, no,”

notes.he: וכי קאמינא דמותר להטיל מום בזמן הזה אמינא:
notes.en: [applies] when the Temple is standing; and when I say it is permitted to inflict a blemish, I say it of the present time.

messages.text: If Rav Yehuda is referring only to today, what is the purpose of stating this halakha? Isn’t it obvious?

Rav Yehuda’s statement is necessary, lest you say: Let us issue a decree against inflicting a blemish on a firstborn fetus, lest most of the fetus’s head emerge from the womb, which is when the sanctity of the firstborn takes effect, and then one inflicts a blemish upon the animal. That would constitute the unlawful infliction of a blemish upon a sacred animal. Rav Yehuda therefore teaches us that such a decree was not issued.

notes.he: וקדיש ליה רחם והדר שדי ביה מומא והוי מטיל מום בקדשים קמ"ל דלא גזרי' דהוא יזהר להטיל בו המום משעה שיצא מעט קודם שיצא רוב ראשו כדאמרינן בבכורות (דף לה.) גדייא באזניה שהגדי יוצא דרך צדעיו ונראות האזנים תחלה ואימרא בשפתיה שפי הטלה יוצא תחלה:
notes.en: Lest most of its head emerge: and the womb sanctifies it, and then he inflicts a blemish on it, and it is inflicting a blemish on sacred animals. It teaches us that we do not decree, for he will take care to inflict the blemish once a little has emerged, before most of its head emerges, as we say in Bekhorot (35a): a kid by its ears, for the kid emerges by way of its temples and the ears appear first; and a lamb by its lips, for the lamb’s mouth emerges first.

messages.text: But one can say that indeed, a decree should be issued prohibiting inflicting a blemish on a fetus due to that concern.

notes.he: דמש"ה ליגזר דלא:
notes.en: And say that indeed: that for this reason we should decree that one may not.

messages.text: Even so, inflicting the blemish on the fetus is preferable to leaving it alone, despite that concern, as otherwise one might come to transgress the prohibitions against shearing the firstborn or working with it. It is prohibited to work or shear a firstborn, even if it is blemished. If the firstborn is born blemished, it may be slaughtered and eaten immediately. By contrast, if it is unblemished, then one must wait for it to become blemished, and there is a concern that one might work or shear the animal in the meantime.

notes.he: למישרי להטיל בו מום הואיל ועדיין לא קדיש כדי שלא יצטרך הכהן לשהותו אלא ימהר לשוחטו דאי לא שדי' בי' בעי לשהויי עד שיפול בו מום ואדהכי והכי אתי לידי גיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: This is preferable: to permit inflicting a blemish on it while it is not yet sanctified, so that the priest will not need to keep it but will hurry to slaughter it. For if he does not inflict a blemish on it, he must keep it until a blemish befalls it, and in the meantime he comes to shearing and work.

notes.he: כלומר שמחסר ממנו אבר קודם יציאת רובו ויעשנו בעל מום:
notes.en: Deficient is preferable [Rashi’s text reads ḥasira, “deficient,” where the printed Gemara reads yatira, “much”]: that is, that he removes a limb from it before most of it emerges and makes it a blemished animal.

notes.dh: הא עדיפא יתירא מדאתי ביה לידי גיזה ועבודה
notes.he: פי' אין בו מום צריך להשהות ואיכא למיחש דלמא אתי לידי תקלה דגיזה ועבודה אבל השתא דיש בו מום שחיט ליה כהן ולא אתי לידי גיזה ועבודה דלמה ישהנו ואר"ת דהשתא נהגו העולם למכור קצת מן האם כדי להפקיע הוולד מן הבכורה וטוב הוא לעשות כן ובלבד שיקנה לו קנין חשוב כמו הגבהה דבהמה דקה או משיכה וקנין כסף עמו ואע"ג דאיכא פ"ק דבכורות (דף ג:) גבי רב מרי בר רחל מקני לעובד כוכבים כו' וכלאי חיותא דרב מרי בר רחל וקאמר עלה דהא דכלאי משום דמפקע להו מכהן והוי איסורא לעשות כן אי אימא משום דרב מרי ידע לאקנויי קנין גמור וכ"ע לא ידעי וסברי דמילתא בעלמא עבד ואתי לידי תקלה ואנן קי"ל כלישנא בתרא דבעיא קנין גמור ואפילו ללשון ראשון נמי ניחא לן טפי למוכרו לעובד כוכבים מלהטיל בו מום קודם יציאת רובו דלא אתי למיטעי להטיל בו מום לאחר יציאת הרוב משום הכי טוב לעשות כן ולמכור קצת מן האם לעובד כוכבים קודם לידה והכי עדיף טפי דלא אתי לידי תקלה דגיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: This is much preferable to his coming to shearing and work: Explanation: if it has no blemish, he must keep it, and there is reason to fear lest he come to the stumbling block of shearing and work; but now that it has a blemish, the priest slaughters it and does not come to shearing and work, for why would he keep it? And Rabbeinu Tam said: nowadays people are accustomed to sell part of the mother [to a gentile] in order to take the offspring out of firstborn status, and it is good to do so, provided that he transfers it to him with a significant act of acquisition, such as lifting, for a small animal, or pulling, together with an acquisition by money. And although in the first chapter of Bekhorot (3b) [it is told] of Rav Mari bar Raḥel, who would transfer [the ears of his animals] to a gentile, etc., and the animals of Rav Mari bar Raḥel died out; and it is said about that, that they died out because he took them away from the priest, and it is forbidden to do so; or else because Rav Mari knew how to transfer a complete acquisition, while not everyone knows, and they think he performed a mere gesture, and they come to a stumbling block. And we hold like the latter version, that a complete acquisition is required. And even according to the first version, we are more comfortable selling it to a gentile than inflicting a blemish on it before most of it emerges, since then he will not come to err and inflict the blemish after most has emerged. Therefore it is good to do so and sell part of the mother to a gentile before the birth; and this is preferable, for he will not come to the stumbling block of shearing and work.

notes.he: להטיל בו מום דאי לא שדי ביה מום דלמא אתי לידי גיזה:
notes.en: Even so, this is preferable: to inflict a blemish on it; for if he does not inflict a blemish on it, perhaps he will come to shearing.

notes.he: דחסירא עדיפא דלא ליתי כו':
notes.en: Another version: this is what Rav Yehuda teaches us: that deficient is preferable [Rabbeinu Gershom too reads ḥasira, “deficient,” for the printed yatira], so that he does not come, etc.

messages.text: Does a female animal become consecrated with firstborn status, such that the owner must designate the fetus as a peace offering in order to circumvent the obligation of the firstborn? The sanctity of the firstborn takes effect only upon male animals.
messages.quote: If it is female, it is designated as a peace offering

notes.he: דבעי לאיערומי עלה דקאמר כיצד מערימין וקחשיב להך:
notes.en: Is a female sanctified as a firstborn: that one would need to employ artifice regarding it? For it says “How does one employ artifice” and counts this case.

messages.text: The latter clause of the mishna comes to discuss the offspring of an animal consecrated as a sin offering. Since the offspring of a sin offering is put to death, the owner may wish to employ artifice to circumvent the sanctity of the mother by consecrating the fetus with a different sanctity.

notes.he: דאם חטאת היא ונתעברה ורוצה להערים שלא ילך למיתה דולד חטאת למיתה אזיל ישנהו לקדושה אחרת וקמ"ל דוולדות קדשים בהוייתן הן קדושים ולא במעי אמן וכיון דעדיין לא קדיש בקדושת אמו מצי לארכובי עליה קדושה אחריתי דלכי מתייליד לא הוי ולד חטאת:
notes.en: To a consecrated animal: that if it is a sin offering and became pregnant, and he wishes to employ artifice so that [the offspring] will not go to its death, since the offspring of a sin offering goes to its death, he changes it to a different sanctity. And it teaches us that the offspring of sacred animals are sacred upon coming into being and not in their mothers’ womb; and since it is not yet sanctified with its mother’s sanctity, he can impose another sanctity on it, so that when it is born it is not the offspring of a sin offering.

notes.he: לשון ירושלמי נקבה מי וכו' במבכרת דקדשים - בבהמת הקדש כדפרישית והאי מבכרת לאו דוקא אלא איידי דתנא רישא במבכרת דחולין נקט נמי הכא לשון מבכרת:
notes.en: The language of the Jerusalem Talmud: “Is a female, etc.? [It refers] to a mevakeret of consecrated animals,” that is, a consecrated animal, as I explained. And the word mevakeret [one giving birth to its firstborn] is not precise here; but since the first clause taught about a non-sacred mevakeret, it uses the word mevakeret here too.

notes.he: אמאי איצטריך למימר נקבה ליהוי חולין נקבה מי מקדש בבכורה] אלא סיפא דקתני ילדה נקבה תמימה תיקרב שלמים בבהמת הקדש קתני דאם הקדיש בהמה מעוברת ואמר ילדה נקבה תהא שלמים הויא שלמים קסבר עובר לאו ירך אמו הוא (ל"א כלישנא קמא) [אמרי הא בהמה מבכרת מאי היא אי דהקדש היא אמאי והשני ימכר האיך דהקדיש עולה כו']:
notes.en: If female, peace offerings: why did it need to say this? A female would be non-sacred anyway; is a female sanctified as a firstborn? Rather, the latter clause, which teaches “if it gave birth to an unblemished female, it shall be sacrificed as peace offerings,” teaches about a consecrated animal: if one consecrated a pregnant animal and said, “If it gives birth to a female, let it be peace offerings,” it is peace offerings. He holds that a fetus is not considered a limb of its mother. (The edition sets aside the words “another version, like the first version,” and adds:) [They say: this animal giving birth to its firstborn, what is it? If it is consecrated, why is the second sold? The one he consecrated as a burnt offering, etc.]

messages.text: If the animal that gave birth to two males was consecrated as a sin offering, then it is understandable that the newborn animal which is consecrated to be a burnt offering should be a burnt offering. But with regard to the other, let it retain the sanctity of its mother. Why does the mishna rule that the money received from its sale is non-sacred?
messages.quote: If the animal gave birth to two males

notes.he: אמאי השני ימכר לחייבי עולה האי קמא דנפיק ליהוי עולה ואידך לכי מתייליד ליהוי בקדושתה דאימיה:
notes.en: If it is a consecrated animal: why is the second sold to those obligated to bring a burnt offering? Let the first one that emerges be a burnt offering, and the other, when it is born, should have its mother’s sanctity.

messages.text: In the last clause of the mishna, we come to the case of a non-sacred animal that is about to give birth to its firstborn.

notes.he: דילדה שני זכרים אתאן לבהמת חולין והוי רישא וסיפא בחולין ומציעתא בהקדש:
notes.en: This latter clause: of “it gave birth to two males,” we come back to a non-sacred animal. So the first clause and the latter clause concern non-sacred animals, and the middle one a consecrated animal.

notes.dh: סיפא אתאן [כאן יש כשתי שורות חלק] לבהמת חולין
notes.he: וכגון דלא ידיעה אהי זכר מינהו אמר עולה הלכך שני ימכר לצרכי עולות ודמיו חולין כדאמרן לעיל:
notes.en: The latter clause comes back [the edition notes a gap of about two lines here] to a non-sacred animal. For example, where it is not known about which of the males he said “a burnt offering”; therefore the second is sold for the needs of burnt offerings and its money is non-sacred, as we said above.

notes.he: ל"א זכר בתרא חולין בעלמא הוא אלא משום דלא ידעינן הי נפקא ברישא הלכך השני ימכר לצרכי עולה ודמיו חולין דמכל מקום לא היה דעתו לעולה אלא על האחד:
notes.en: Another version: the latter male is merely non-sacred; but since we do not know which emerged first, the second is sold for the needs of a burnt offering and its money is non-sacred, for in any case his intention for a burnt offering was only for one.

messages.text: The mishna teaches: If the animal gave birth to a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: They are not imbued with sanctity. This indicates that they are not imbued with sanctity in any case, even if they are the offspring of a consecrated animal.
messages.quote: If the animal gave birth to a tumtum … or a hermaphrodite

messages.text: Continues on 25a: the Gemara asks why they are not imbued with the sanctity of their mother, and answers that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that the offspring of sacrificial animals are sanctified only as they come into being.
